title_as_printed: Longitudinal changes of blood β-synuclein in cognitively unimpaired, mild cognitive impairment and sporadic Alzheimer´s disease
blind_code_notes: Task: T2 arguable (single-marker AUC 0.90 for MCI converters vs stable). The preliminary blind record set is_model_study=false; on reflection it is set true because, under the template's own wording ('a classifier, a diagnostic model or a cut-point'), the study evaluates single-biomarker cut-points by ROC (AUC, sensitivity/specificity at a threshold) without fitting a multivariable model or validating. Either way V2 is correct.

registry_codes.Sample_N_Approx: 463 ADNI participants (135 CU + 166 MCI + 162 AD); 235 with at least one follow-up serum; CSF AD biomarkers for 194; β-synuclein-vs-NRGN comparison subset 148.

Task_Type.reason: Two honest readings. The stated aim and title are a longitudinal characterisation of a serum biomarker (group comparisons, rate of change, correlations), which is T4. But the paper also evaluates a beta-synuclein cut-point for MCI-to-dementia conversion with AUC, sensitivity and specificity, and headlines conversion prediction in the abstract and conclusions, which supports T2.
Task_Type.quote: β-Synuclein discriminated MCI (Aβ+) converters from stable MCI (Aβ+) with an AUC of 0.90 (95% CI 0.78–1.00, Fig. 1G) and a sensitivity and specificity of 76.9% and 100% (threshold 10.3 pg/mL). [p.4] / The aim of the present study was to characterize serum β-synuclein levels in longitudinal samples from participants of the Alzheimer´s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) at different stages of AD [p.2]
